column2: She accepted the compliment, but his condescension made the praise sting.
column3: 她接受了讚美，但他那種居高臨下的態度讓這番稱讚刺耳。
column4: speak with condescension (帶著傲慢說話)
column5: condescend 屈尊俯就 + sion：名詞就是那副高高在上的神態

column2: A pervasive sense of dread hung over the town before the storm.
column3: 暴風雨來臨前，一股揮之不去的恐懼籠罩著整座小鎮。
column5: per 穿過 + vas 走：到處穿行，哪裡都走得到

column2: Rainwater slowly began to permeate the thin soil and reach the roots.
column3: 雨水慢慢開始滲入薄薄的土壤，到達根部。
column4: smoke permeates the air (煙霧瀰漫空氣)
column5: per 穿過 + meate 走：像水一樣穿過縫隙滲進去

column2: The textbook's elucidation of the theory finally made the proof clear.
column3: 教科書對這個理論的闡明，終於讓證明變得清楚易懂。
column4: elucidation of a point (闡明要點)
column5: e 出 + lucid 清楚（像 lucky 運氣的光）：講到完全明白

column2: The coalescence of small streams into one river carved the broad valley.
column3: 小溪匯聚成一條大河，切出了寬闊的山谷。
column5: co 一起 + alesc 成長：小東西長在一起變成一個

column2: The new bridge design came under intense scrutiny from independent engineers.
column3: 新橋的設計受到獨立工程師的嚴格審視。
column5: 想像放大鏡底下，連最小的細節都逃不掉

column2: Her essay offers a synthesis of three rival theories in one clear model.
column3: 她的文章把三種互相競爭的理論統整成一個清楚的模型。
column4: a synthesis of ideas (想法的綜合)
column5: syn 一起 + thesis 放置：把各部分放在一起

column2: Pragmatism, not ideology, guided the mayor when she repaired the city's budget.
column3: 市長整頓市府預算時，指引她的是務實精神，而非意識形態。
column5: prag 做事（像 practice 實踐）：只看行不行得通

column2: A benevolent donor quietly paid for the village school's new library.
column3: 一位仁慈的捐款者默默出錢，替村裡的學校蓋了新圖書館。
column5: bene 好 + vol 意願（像 volunteer 志願者）：心懷善意

column2: Visitors remembered the old doctor's benevolence long after he retired.
column3: 來訪者在老醫生退休很久之後，仍記得他的仁慈。
column5: bene 好 + vol 意願：願望是善良的，就是仁愛

column2: Scientists stayed dubious about the claim because no lab could repeat the test.
column3: 由於沒有實驗室能重做這項測試，科學家對這個說法仍存疑。
column5: du 二（像 double）：心裡有兩個想法，半信半疑

column2: Her idiosyncratic teaching style included singing the periodic table to the class.
column3: 她獨具個人特色的教學風格，包括對全班唱出元素週期表。
column5: idio 自己（像 idiom 慣用語）：只屬於自己的怪特色

column2: Wearing mismatched socks was one of the professor's harmless idiosyncrasies.
column3: 穿不成對的襪子是教授無傷大雅的怪癖之一。
column5: idio 自己：只有他自己才有的小習慣
column7: id - i - o - syn - cra - sy

column2: The film triggered a visceral reaction of fear in the audience before they could think.
column3: 這部電影在觀眾還來不及思考之前，就引發了發自本能的恐懼反應。
column5: 想像肚子深處一緊，不用腦袋想就先有感覺

column2: The dogmatic editor refused to consider any view but his own.
column3: 那位固執武斷的編輯拒絕考慮自己以外的任何看法。
column5: dogma 教條 + tic：像死抱教條不放的人

column2: Galileo challenged old dogma when he argued that Earth moves around the sun.
column3: 伽利略主張地球繞著太陽轉，挑戰了舊有的教條。
column5: dog 狗媽媽 ma 說不准動：一條不准質疑的死規定

column2: Gold is so malleable that it can be hammered into paper-thin sheets.
column3: 黃金延展性極佳，可以被搥打成薄如紙的金屬片。
column5: mall 槌子（像 mallet 木槌）：一敲就能變形

column2: The malleability of young minds makes early education especially powerful.
column3: 年輕心智的可塑性，使早期教育格外有力量。
column4: malleability of metal (金屬的延展性)
column5: malleable 可塑的 + ity：名詞就是可塑的程度
column7: mal - le - a - bil - i - ty

column2: Engineers need a viable plan that fits both the budget and the schedule.
column3: 工程師需要一個同時符合預算與時程的可行計畫。
column5: vi 生命（像 vital）+ able：能活下去，就行得通

column2: Investors doubted the viability of a business that lost money every month.
column3: 投資人懷疑一家每月虧損的企業是否有生存發展的能力。
column5: viable 能活的 + ity：事業活不活得下去

column2: The duck's oily feathers are impervious to rain.
column3: 鴨子油亮的羽毛不受雨水影響，水滲不進去。
column4: impervious to criticism (不受批評影響)
column5: im 不 + per 穿過 + via 路：沒有路能穿過去

column2: With the ubiquity of smartphones, almost anyone can record an event instantly.
column3: 由於智慧型手機無所不在，幾乎任何人都能立刻記錄事件。
column5: ubi 在哪裡：問哪裡有，答案是哪裡都有

column2: Students stayed deferential to the elderly professor and rose when he entered.
column3: 學生對年長的教授十分恭敬，他一進來就起立。
column5: defer 聽從 + ential：低頭聽從長輩的

column2: She gave a disdainful sniff at the plain, handmade gift.
column3: 她對那份樸素的手作禮物不屑地哼了一聲。
column5: disdain 鄙視 + ful：充滿鄙視的樣子

column2: An eminent physicist was invited to give the opening lecture.
column3: 一位傑出的物理學家受邀發表開場演講。
column5: e 出 + min 突出（像 prominent）：高高突出人群的人

column2: The architect rose to eminence after designing the city's famous concert hall.
column3: 這位建築師在設計了該市著名的音樂廳之後聲名大噪。
column5: eminent 顯赫 + ce：站上高處的地位

column2: She caught only a fleeting glimpse of the fox before it vanished.
column3: 她只匆匆瞥見那隻狐狸一眼，牠就消失了。
column5: flee 逃走：一下子就逃掉、溜走了

column2: Travelers crossed the hostile desert, where water and shade were almost impossible to find.
column3: 旅人橫越嚴酷的沙漠，那裡幾乎找不到水和遮蔭。
column5: hostile 長得像 host 主人，卻是不歡迎你的主人

column2: Open hostility between the two families made the wedding awkward.
column3: 兩個家族之間公然的敵意，讓婚禮氣氛尷尬。
column5: hostile 敵對的 + ity：名詞就是敵意

column2: An intricate pattern of tiny birds covered the silk.
column3: 細小鳥兒交織成的錯綜精細圖案覆蓋了整塊絲綢。
column5: 想像一團細密交織的蕾絲，每條線都纏在一起

column2: Students admired the intricacy of the antique clock's tiny gears.
column3: 學生們讚嘆古董鐘裡小齒輪的繁複精細。
column5: intricate 的名詞，一堆小齒輪層層交錯

column2: A malicious rumor spread through the school and hurt her reputation.
column3: 一則惡意的謠言在學校傳開，傷害了她的名聲。
column5: mal 壞（像 malfunction 故障）+ ous：壞心眼的

column2: He felt no malice toward his rival and even shook her hand.
column3: 他對對手毫無惡意，甚至和她握了手。
column5: mal 壞：壞念頭，想害人的心

column2: Floppy disks are now obsolete because cloud storage replaced them.
column3: 軟碟如今已經過時，因為雲端儲存取代了它們。
column5: 想像傳呼機被丟進博物館，被時代淘汰

column2: Rapid obsolescence of phones leads many people to replace them every two years.
column3: 手機快速過時，使許多人每兩年就換新機。
column5: obsolete 過時 + escence：漸漸變得過時的過程

column2: The prolific novelist published nearly two books every year.
column3: 這位多產的小說家幾乎每年出版兩本書。
column5: pro 向前 + lific 生產：不斷生出新作品

column2: The senator moved to repudiate the claim, calling it completely false.
column3: 那位參議員出面駁斥這項說法，稱它完全不實。
column5: 想像把說法退回去並大喊「我不認！」

column2: The company's swift repudiation of the rumor calmed its investors.
column3: 公司迅速駁斥謠言，安撫了投資人。
column5: repudiate 的名詞，把說法退回去的動作

column2: The soldiers stood in solemn silence as the flag was lowered.
column3: 旗幟降下時，士兵們在莊嚴的靜默中肅立。
column5: 結尾 mn 的 n 不發音，和 column 一樣

column2: The solemnity of the ceremony silenced even the youngest children.
column3: 典禮的莊嚴肅穆，連最小的孩子也安靜下來。
column5: solemn 的 n 不發音，但 solemnity 的 n 要唸出來
